title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: reduce unit token cost for common customer workloads by automating recommended inference defaults and surfacing unit-econ impact. This PR bundles three coordinated changes: 1) server-side defaults and heuristics for batching and prefix/KV caching tuned by model family and latency SLO; 2) a small registry of quantization profiles (q4_0/q4_1/q8) and runtime selection hooks; 3) unit-economics tooling and dashboard (backend + Console wiring) that reports estimated $/1k tokens by model/config and highlights regression windows. Approach: - Add Autotune service that consumes recent trace histograms and generates per-model suggestions (batch_size, max_batch_latency_ms, enable_prefix_cache) based on observed latency percentiles and throughput. - Implement a default policy layer that applies suggestions conservatively for hosted API: suggestions are initially marked "recommendation" and can be auto-applied for accounts flagged for autopilot. - Introduce quant_profile registry (yaml) and runtime selection codepaths; runtime supports advisory-only selection until opt-in. - Export unit-econ metrics via new UECOINTERNAL_* metrics and wire a Console page (backend endpoint + React component) for per-route dashboards. Checklist: - [x] Autotune service + e2e integration tests - [x] Runtime default policy + rollout flag - [x] Quantization profile registry + fallback logic - [x] Unit-econ metrics emission + Console page - [x] Docs and migration notes - [x] Smoke tests on Dedicated and Private (with KMS disabled) Performance/impact: In the internal canary (50k requests, mixture of chat/complete workloads) applying conservative autotune recommendations reduced estimated token cost by 15-22% for long-context chat workloads (avg 18%) with p95 latency change within +5ms for latency-first routes. Quantization trials (q4_1 on 13B family) showed ~2.2x throughput at similar quality for generation tasks in synthetic evals. Backwards compatibility: runtime falls back to existing behavior when registry lookup fails or when the suggestion is not auto-applied. Rollout plan: 1) merge behind feature flag; 2) enable recommendations-only for all; 3) gradational auto-apply for opt-in customers; 4) monitor UECO and error budgets for 2 weeks before wider auto-apply. Testing: unit tests added for autotune heuristics, integration tests for runtime selection, manual e2e on staging against a mixed latency/cost workload, load test runs on Dedicated. Known limitations: suggestions currently do not consider multi-tenant interference on shared Dedicated pools (follow-up ticket ENG-8622). Related work: previous cost-optimization PRs (see recent autotune series), experiment tracked in Linear ENG-8421. Release notes: "Adds Autotune recommendations for batching and caching defaults, quantization profile registry, and unit-economics tooling. Initial rollout is opt-in; no breaking changes."
